verdict.line: You lose if you let the lane turn into extended auto trades once Jax hits 6 and his Counter Strike (E) is up; you win if you land your stun combo while Fury is above 50 before that E comes off cooldown.

brief.thesis: Renekton's stun pressure from Q (Cull the Meek), W (Ruthless Predator), and E (Slice and Dice) is front-loaded and punishes short-trade windows before level 6, while Jax's Counter Strike (E) and Relentless Assault (R) reward exactly the kind of prolonged auto-attack fight Renekton should avoid once Jax hits 6. The 50.2% win rate over 2815 games reflects two kits with opposite timing windows rather than a clear favorite — Renekton owns the engage, Jax owns the extended fight.

theirWindow.what: His Counter Strike dodges all incoming basic attacks for its duration and then stuns and damages everyone around him, so an all-in into an up E gets your autos negated and you eat a free stun. Hold your empowered W (the 3-hit version) and wait him out instead of forcing it into that window.

yourWindow.when: Fury over 50, his E on cooldown
yourWindow.what: At 50+ Fury your W becomes three slashes that strip shields and stun for 1.5s instead of 0.75s, and your Q and E both hit harder with E also shredding Armor. Commit the full Q-E-W string the instant you see his E go down, especially before he hits level 6 and unlocks Relentless Assault.

runes.keystoneWhy: 48.5% win rate at 43.2% pick — Conqueror's stacking adaptive damage and the healing on full stacks reward the exact short, repeated trades your Q heal and stun combo create.

summoners.why: 81.3% pick rate at 50.4% win rate — Ignite punishes Jax's lack of sustain in the short trade windows your stun combo creates before his Counter Strike resets.

playing.title: Track your own Fury, not just his cooldowns
playing.detail: Your Q, W, and E all get materially stronger above 50 Fury — W specifically goes from two slashes with a 0.75s stun to three slashes that strip shields and stun for 1.5s. Build Fury in safe exchanges before you commit the real combo.

playing.title: Never W into an active Counter Strike
playing.detail: His E dodges all incoming basic attacks and then stuns and damages everyone around him. Your empowered W's follow-up autos get voided by this, so hold the combo until his E visibly goes down.

playing.title: All-in before level 6
playing.detail: His E is 18 seconds at rank 1 and he has no Relentless Assault yet, so your W-stun into Q-E window has no clean punish. This is your single best all-in period of the lane.

playing.title: Punish his Leap Strike engage
playing.detail: Once he commits Q to leap onto you, he has no second gap-closer or escape besides that same ability on cooldown. Land your W stun immediately after the leap lands to lock in the trade.

playing.title: Watch his stacks before you commit
playing.detail: Check his Conqueror or passive stacking before engaging — a fully stacked Jax heals or hits significantly harder on the trade, so bait a bad E usage from him first if you can.

playing.title: Avoid extended auto trades past level 6
playing.detail: Relentless Assault gives him free attack speed on every strike with bonus damage every third hit, so standing and trading autos past a few seconds favors him. Land your burst and disengage instead of staying in range.

playing.title: Use E to reset the fight, not just engage
playing.detail: Slice and Dice's dash can reposition you out of his attack-speed window just as easily as it closes distance. Don't treat it as a one-way commit button once his R is active.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the timing windows, stun interactions, and trade advice are my own read of the ability text, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful not to use Renekton’s reinforced [W] while Jax has Counter Strike (E) active. Keep an eye out on Jax’s Conqueror and (P) stacks before engaging combat.
